title: Per-head precision staging and bulk-dequant amortizer for streaming prefill scheduling
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Dequantization overhead is a dominant tail cost for mixed-precision attention when using INT8/FP8 model paths, especially for streaming prefill workloads where many short requests share prefixes. We need a runtime strategy that reduces repeated per-request dequant work and enables per-head precision transitions without violating latency SLOs or increasing peak memory significantly.

Goal: Implement a per-head precision staging mechanism that allows different attention heads to run at different precisions during prefill/decode and a bulk-dequant amortizer that aggregates and reuses dequantized weights/activations across microbatches and concurrent prefix reuse. The feature should integrate with kernel selection so the runtime can pick optimized INT8/FP8 kernels where beneficial and fall back to FP16/FP32 for sensitive heads.

Scope: runtime kernel selection changes, attention execution path changes (per-head), prefill scheduler hooks for amortized dequant, telemetry and benchmarks, and a small opt-in config flag in model profile for experimental rollout.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration that reduces per-token dequant CPU/GPU overhead by at least 30% in representative streaming prefill traces (measured end-to-end on dedicated GPU pool)
No more than 5% regression in log-probability (quality) on our internal eval prompt set for models with per-head mixed precision enabled
Kernel selector can route heads to INT8/FP8/FP16 kernels based on per-head scoring and constexpr thresholds
Prefill scheduler reuses amortized dequant artifacts across at least 3 concurrent microbatches and exposes metrics for reuse hit rate
Feature can be toggled per-model via model profile and rolled out gradually via canary in Console
design_notes: Per-head staging: represent attention heads as groups with precision tag. During prefill we annotate KV cache entries with head-precision metadata so decode kernels can pick mixed-precision execution without reshaping weight tensors at runtime.

Bulk-dequant amortizer: maintain a short-lived LRU keyed by (model_version, weight_blob_id, quant_params_hash) that stores dequantized tensors in GPU memory for reuse across concurrent requests and short-lived prefill windows.

Kernel selector: extend existing kernel scoring to consider head grouping, dequant amortizer presence (reuse hit reduces effective cost), and expected decode sequence length to decide between INT8/FP8 fastpath vs FP16 fallback.
Memory accounting: amortizer entries must be evictable and accounted to model's reserved memory quota to avoid OOM on multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

Prefill scheduling hooks: scheduler will attempt to batch prefill steps across inflight requests that share prefix hashes; when batching fails, amortizer must still provide benefit for short reuse windows.
Telemetry: add counters for amortizer hits/misses, per-head precision assignments, dequant time breakdown, and kernel-choice telemetry for post-deploy analysis.
tradeoffs: Pros: Significant reduction in repeated dequant cost and lower tail latency for many short streaming requests that share prefixes; allows aggressive INT8/FP8 use where safe per-head.

Cons: Increased GPU memory footprint for cached dequant tensors; added complexity in KV cache metadata and kernel selection heuristics; potential for quality regressions if per-head quant decisions are too aggressive.
Mitigations: strict memory caps on amortizer, conservative default thresholds, and eval-based per-model profiles that record head-sensitivity to precision changes.
implementation_plan: 1) Add per-head precision metadata to attention op and KV cache format (runtime schema migration with backwards compatibility flag)
2) Implement lightweight in-GPU amortizer cache with eviction and API for kernel consumers to pin/unpin entries
3) Extend kernel selector to accept per-head scoring vector and amortizer availability hint; update candidate cost model to include amortizer hit probability
4) Modify prefill scheduler to surface microbatch/ prefix grouping opportunities to amortizer and to prefer grouped execution when it reduces dequant cost
5) Add config toggles: model_profile.mixed_precision_staging: enum {off, conservative, aggressive} and model_profile.amortizer_enabled: boolean
6) Instrument telemetry and a set of synthetic and production-like benchmarks
7) Run canary on non-critical tenant pool, analyze metrics, iterate thresholds and eviction policy
8) Gradual rollout with runtime dashboard and automatic rollback on SLO/quality regressions.
benchmarks: Synthetic perf: streaming prefill trace generator (prefill_len=32, bursty arrivals) used to validate 30-45% GPU kernel time reduction with amortizer hit rate ~0.6
Quality eval: internal 'prefill-safety' prompt set for quant-sensitive heads, default conservative profile target <5% log-prob degradation
Cost projection: expected 12-20% overall token-cost reduction for heavy streaming workloads once amortizer stabilizes
Benchmark notes: run on Dedicated p3-standard-equivalent pool; repeat measurements with and without amortizer for 50k requests to get stable hit-rate estimates.
